description:
Return each player and the date the streak started. Query:
  sql/queries/scenario2_ipl_30plus_streaks.sql. Every run loads
  sql/schema/02_ipl.sql and sql/seed/02_ipl.sql into PostgreSQL 18 (PGlite).
  The scores are synthetic; each player in the seed exists to prove one rule.
  Expected rows come from an independent TypeScript oracle that reads the raw
  tables and walks each player's 2024 innings in date order.

elements.name: The query returns exactly the streaks worked out by hand

steps.name: the "IPL 2024" SQL scenario is loaded
I run the scenario query
the result columns should be "player_name, streak_start_date, streak_end_date, streak_length"

cells: a 5-match streak is one row, not three 3-match windows
exactly 3 matches, the last one exactly 30 runs
first of two streaks in the season
second streak after a duck: both are reported
a match the player did not bat in is skipped
rows inserted newest-first are ordered by date

steps.name: the result should be exactly these streaks, worked out by hand:
the result should match the independent oracle

cells: a 29 breaks what would otherwise be a 5-match run
four 30+ scores, never two in a row
36, 52 at the end of 2023 and 41, 33 at the start of 2024
a tail-ender with gaps and ducks

elements.description:
The anti-pattern uses LAG/LEAD ("this innings and the ones either side are
    30+") and filters the season after the window. The oracle check must reject it.

I run the anti-pattern query "scenario2_lag_lead_windows"
the result should not match the independent oracle
the result should have 11 rows
"Virat Kohli" should appear in exactly 3 rows
"Shubman Gill" should have a streak from "2023-05-18" to "2024-03-31" of 3 matches

description:
Account A sends money to account B, and B sends a similar amount (within 10%)
  back to A within 24 hours. Query: sql/queries/scenario1_round_trip_transfers.sql.
  Every run loads sql/schema/01_transactions.sql and sql/seed/01_transactions.sql
  into PostgreSQL 18 (PGlite, in-process). Expected rows come from an independent
  TypeScript oracle that reads the raw transactions and applies the same rules
  with integer paise and integer seconds, so the boundaries are exact.

elements.name: The query returns exactly the round trips worked out by hand

steps.name: the "round-trip transfers" SQL scenario is loaded
I run the scenario query
the result columns should be "account_a, account_b, sent_txn_id, sent_amount, sent_at, returned_txn_id, returned_amount, returned_at, hours_apart, pct_difference"

cells: same amount sent back 2.5 hours later
the earlier transfer is A, even when its account sorts last
second of two qualifying returns: both pairs are reported
chain A to B to A to B, first round trip
chain A to B to A to B, the return starts a new round trip

steps.name: the result should be exactly these round trips, worked out by hand:
the result should match the independent oracle

cells: sent back 24 hours and 1 second later
10% less and one paisa more (17999.99 on 20000)
10% more and one paisa more (22000.01 on 20000)
same pair read backwards: the return must come after
a round trip is reported once, never again with A and B swapped
self-transfers (from = to) are not round trips
a triangle A to B to C to A never sends money straight back
only 5% of the amount comes back

steps.name: the seed should hold these near misses, and none of them should be reported:

elements.description:
The anti-pattern compares times with ABS() instead of "strictly later" and
    drops the self-transfer filter. The oracle check must reject it.
elements.name: A plausible but wrong query is caught by the same checks

the result should not match the independent oracle
the result should have 23 rows
sent transfer "TX0102" and return "TX0101" should be reported
sent transfer "TX0801" and return "TX0802" should be reported
sent transfer "TX0603" and return "TX0601" should be reported
